summary.headline: KDDL standalone Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose 87.6% YoY to INR36.4 crore at a 25.1% margin; FY26 standalone revenue INR506 crore, up 31.9%.
summary.overview: Management reported standalone Q4 FY26 total income of INR145.3 crore (up ~42% YoY) and PAT of INR19.8 crore (13.6% margin). Consolidated Q4 total income was ~INR585 crore (up ~35.6%) with PAT of INR34.5 crore, and consolidated FY26 revenue reached INR2,207.8 crore (up ~30.3%). Watch components (ex-Ethos, ex-bracelets) grew ~20% to ~INR240 crore, Precision Engineering (Eigen) grew 35%+ to ~INR200 crore, and Ornapac grew ~37% to INR23 crore. Management guided to a 25% medium-term CAGR for bracelets and precision engineering, slightly lower for watch components, and no major margin change this year.

segments.name: Watch components (dials, hands)
segments.commentary: Revenue ~INR240 crore vs INR200 crore last year, ~20% growth. Recovered in H2 FY26 after a quiet H1; management expects H1 FY27 export roughly stable and growth more visible in H2.

segments.name: Bracelets
segments.commentary: Revenue ~INR40 crore, export-led, reported separately from the INR240 crore watch component figure. Capacity utilisation ~75-80% on existing capacity; expects 20-25% growth.

segments.name: Precision Engineering (Eigen)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ~INR200 crore vs INR147 crore, up 35%+. Expansion underway with backward integration into plating and some capacity additions; Bangalore-related capex expected to commission in 3-4 months.

segments.name: Ornapac (packaging)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR23 crore vs ~INR17 crore, up ~37%. Still loss-making during ramp-up; management expects profitability in H2 FY27.

segments.name: Ethos (retail, subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Crossed 100 boutiques in FY26; management targets doubling the network in ~3 years and revenue growth of 20-25% p.a. Results were declared a week before the call; no Ethos financials were detailed on the call.

segments.name: Favre-Leuba (Silvercity Brands, Switzerland)
segments.commentary: Present in 20+ countries with 80+ points of sale; sales well above plan and stores short of stock. Management expects sales to more than double in FY27. Not disclosed in financial terms.

guidance_outlook: Precision Engineering and bracelets: ~25% medium-to-long-term value CAGR; watch components slightly lower.
Bracelets: good revenue growth in FY27 and FY28, with margins moderating near term as newer, lower-price customers ramp.
Favre-Leuba: sales expected to more than double in FY27.
Ornapac: expected to turn profitable in H2 FY27.
Capex of ~INR50 crore planned for FY27 across standalone businesses (bracelets, watch components, precision engineering, packaging); excludes subsidiaries such as Favre-Leuba.
No major change in margin picture expected this year; currency tailwind from CHF expected to persist at similar levels.

Ethos: aims to double store network in ~3 years (Pranav Saboo said it may take 4); a new format at INR25,000-2 lakh price point is planned this year; Swiss franc pricing gap of ~7-8% expected to be passed on over time.
risks_watch: Weak Swiss luxury watch demand in China and Europe could keep H1 FY27 export growth flat.
Margin pressure from lower price points of new bracelet customers and from Ethos Swiss franc pricing lag.
Ornapac must reach profitability in H2 FY27 as guided.
Eigen expansion timing (commissioning in 3-4 months) and customer concentration in the busbar OEM.
Bracelet customer concentration, flagged by an analyst; management says new customers are being added.
Ethos store expansion and working capital (inventory days ~221) need monitoring.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and results, but evasive on granular disclosures: volume, currency-adjusted numbers, Favre-Leuba financials, bracelet peak capacity and capex asset turns were not shared. Management was cautious on near-term export demand and on margin direction for this year.
key_quotes: It is in our nature in our DNA to be cautious in our promises, but aggressive enough performance.
We expect to more than double the sales in FY27 and greatly expand our global footprint with exciting new product launches.

Eigen as such is not a product selling company. For Eigen, it does not matter whether it's a busbar or some other component for some other applications, we continue to remain a capability selling company.

qa_highlights.question: Is bracelet revenue part of the INR240 crore watch component figure, and what is its size?
qa_highlights.answer: Bracelets are separate from the INR240 crore watch component figure; bracelet revenue is around INR40 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the standalone volume growth versus value growth, and is the INR50 crore capex for standalone only or including Favre-Leuba?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify volume growth, saying volumes across products are too disparate to sum. The INR50 crore capex covers standalone businesses (bracelets, watch components, precision engineering, packaging) and excludes subsidiaries such as Favre-Leuba.

qa_highlights.question: What is the bracelet utilisation level and how will it ramp, and are new customers being won?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing bracelet capacity was about 75-80% utilised this year; capacity is being added incrementally, and new customers are being added, so utilisation is expected to rise this year.

qa_highlights.question: Will Eigen's Bangalore capex commission soon, and is the new capex backed by orders or OEM visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: The Eigen capex started last year is still in progress; backward integration of processes is expected to be commissioned in the next 3-4 months. Management described Eigen as a capability-selling company, not dependent on the busbar product.

qa_highlights.question: Will the standalone margin improve as store expansion costs in Ethos mature, and what drove the Q4 margin jump?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Ethos store costs are already in the P&L and the expansion continues; margin direction depends on currency and price pass-through. For standalone, the CFO said margins are expected to stay in the same band with no dramatic change, and the currency benefit has run through the full year.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Swiss franc move has Ethos passed on, and how much remains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pricing is roughly 7-8% below required levels, with the gap to be passed on over time, typically every six months, since about 50 brands decide prices comparatively.

capex_capacity: Planned capex of ~INR50 crore for FY27 across standalone businesses (bracelets, watch components, precision engineering, packaging), including maintenance and growth capex; excludes subsidiary investments such as Favre-Leuba. Management said major part goes to Precision Engineering and bracelets.
Capex of ~INR34 crore invested in FY26 across divisions (standalone).
Eigen (precision engineering) capex started last year is still in progress; backward integration into plating (previously outsourced) expected to be commissioned in the next 3-4 months.

Bracelet capacity: ~75,000 units approximate original capacity; utilisation ~75-80% on existing capacity in FY26; management plans to expand to ~110,000-120,000 units over the next 12 months; capacity added incrementally and measured in value rather than units.

Management declined to give peak-utilisation revenue for bracelet and packaging capacities, Eigen capacity before/after expansion, Favre-Leuba size, or asset turns on capex, citing confidentiality and mix-driven capacity.
demand_pricing: Watch components (dials, hands) recovered in H2 FY26 after a quiet H1; management expects H1 FY27 export business roughly stable with growth more visible in H2 FY27; domestic business expected robust. Management said growth could exceed 11-12% if global luxury watch demand improves.

Weak luxury demand in China and parts of Europe; global brands cautious on inventory and procurement; Swiss watches face headwinds in several markets. Customer diversification beyond Switzerland to brands at different price points underway; Switzerland still largest by value.

Bracelets: export-led, ~INR40 crore revenue FY26 (separate from INR240 crore watch components); good revenue growth expected FY27 and FY28 with near-term margin moderation from lower price-point new customers. Management guides 20-25% growth; steel remains ~80% of metal bracelets globally; other metals not ruled out.

Precision Engineering (Eigen): FY26 revenue ~INR200 crore vs INR147 crore (35%+); growth from deeper existing customer relationships, new customers and new products; export focus; EV, energy storage and electronics named as priority sectors. Management says Eigen's precision-stamping market share is very small.
Ornapac packaging: FY26 revenue INR23 crore vs ~INR17 crore (~37%); supplies to international brands for the domestic market began; loss-making in ramp-up, expected profitable in H2 FY27.

Pricing and margins: management guides no major change in margin picture this year; CHF strength is a tailwind expected to persist at similar levels; Ethos Swiss franc pricing gap of ~7-8% expected to be passed on over time (roughly every six months, across ~50 brands). Standalone margin rise partly attributed to CHF strength per CFO.

adds.what: Bracelet capacity expansion from ~75,000 to ~110,000-120,000 units
Eigen (precision engineering) backward integration into plating, Bangalore-related capex

growth.why: Management guides ~25% value CAGR for bracelets and precision engineering, slightly lower for watch components (11-12% dials growth), and Favre-Leuba sales to more than double in FY27; backing is partial, with bracelet capacity to ~110-120k units over 12 months, Eigen plating commissioning in 3-4 months and ~INR50 cr FY27 capex, but no capacity numbers were given for Eigen or Favre-Leuba.
